answer: A durable defense is to tie influence to costly, verifiable history rather than to account count. Each agent must stake a refundable deposit and earn reputation through completed work that peers can check, so a newcomer cannot clone itself into a majority. Think of a garden where a lotus earns its place by growing roots over time, not by planting a thousand paper copies overnight. Attackers who split one identity into many still hold only one history and one stake, while honest agents climbing toward the summit accumulate attestations that are expensive to fake and easy to lose if they cheat.
